task: MAP #18 (first half): deploys never change files under a run in progress — deploy into a new release folder and switch a 'current' link atomically; rerunning only Changed Steps is held for horizon 18.

analysis.objective: Make Promotion safe while runs are in progress (horizon 17, first half of MAP #18): every stage and prod deploy copies the new version into its own releases/<commit> folder inside the Server folder and switches a relative 'current' link in one atomic step, and every run locks onto the folder it started in, so files under a run in progress never change. Deploys still run every Pipeline; rerunning only Changed Steps is horizon 18.
analysis.successDefinition: Done when ALL hold, each proved by a unit test that parses the generated YAML (g7) or by code covered 100% line+branch with no new pragma (g2/g5), plus one e2e case inside the 20-minute job (g4): (1) adops-stage.yml and adops-prod.yml never run git fetch/checkout into the live Server folder and never compose up/down/restart/stop/start; they validate, run `adops server-release` with the validated checkout mounted read-only at /checkout, reload `adops.interface.server:defs`, then run every Pipeline from /project/current. (2) Bind mount, compose project directory and compose project name are unchanged by a switch, so Dagster run history and demo data survive. (3) A run resolves 'current' once at start and reads adops.yaml, pipelines/, pipelines/accepted/, .env and the dbt tree only from that folder for its whole life, retries included; one e2e case holds a scheduled stage run, deploys a new commit, and shows the held run finishes on the old files and fingerprint while the next run uses the new ones. (4) After a switch, every release folder except the newest 3, the current one and any folder a run in progress uses is deleted; a run in progress never loses its folder (the e2e makes ≥3 newer folders so this is really tested). (5) server-release stops before changing any file on the old or half-moved layout, and when the new commit's docker-compose.yml or server/*.yaml differ from the live top-level copies, each time naming the matching section of docs/playbooks/promotion.md, which gives the one-time manual move and the manual config-update step. (6) ADR-0016 has a dated clarification; promotion.md, run-stage-and-prod-on-a-mac.md and the workflow headers describe the new flow. (7) Plain and demo templates change together, templates ship in the wheel (g3), ruff passes (g1).
assumptions: confirmed: deploy way is a new folder, then a switch. Each version is checked out into releases/<commit> inside the Server folder. A 'current' link is switched in one atomic step. Each run resolves the link once at run start, so an old run finishes on old files while new runs use new ones. Deploys never wait for the Server to be idle.

confirmed: the horizon-8 decision 'merge→stage runs every Pipeline, not only changed ones' is replaced. Stage AND prod deploys rerun only Changed Steps, prod starts saving its own Step Fingerprints in prod's Warehouse, and a deploy with no saved fingerprints runs everything.

confirmed: changes that alter no fingerprint use safe defaults. A new accepted-change record reruns that Pipeline in full, any adops.yaml change reruns every Pipeline, a Pipeline with no Schedule still runs in full on every deploy, and otherwise each Pipeline reruns from its first Changed Step.

confirmed: existing Servers move to the new layout by one-time manual steps in docs/playbooks/promotion.md, done while idle. A deploy that finds the old layout stops with a clear message that points there.
confirmed: old releases/<commit> folders are cleaned up after a switch. The deploy deletes all but the newest 3 and keeps any folder a run in progress still uses.

The switch happens inside the stable bind mount: the Server folder stays the compose project directory and the mount source, and only /project/current changes. This avoids a container restart (ADR-0014 / promotion.md forbid one) and keeps the compose project name and volumes. The link is relative, so it resolves the same on the host and in the container.

'Changed Steps' keeps its existing meaning: rerun from the first Step whose (name, fingerprint) differs, in Step order. There is no dependency graph. This reuses first_changed_step and run_pipeline's existing `first` slicing, using the Environment's default schemas rather than Branch schemas.

'An adops.yaml change' and 'a new accepted-change record' are found by comparing against state saved in that Environment's Warehouse adops schema at the last deploy: a hash of adops.yaml, and the record ids found in pipelines/accepted/ compared with ids already applied or seen. Git diff is not used, because ADR-0006 / the h6 decision rule out Git for Changed Steps. A record the Environment has already applied is not new.
A Pipeline with no Changed Step is skipped and gets a Run Log line saying nothing changed. It is not run.

The deploy's own changed-only run runs from the newly switched releases/<commit> folder (with the shared .env and .adops/), resolved once, under the existing per-Pipeline Warehouse lock. It still bypasses the QueuedRunCoordinator, as today.

.env and .adops/ (dlt state and Incremental cursors, DuckDB files and locks, Run Logs, compute logs) stay one shared copy at the Server folder root. Every release folder reaches them by symlink or by an overlay mount. Runtime files Dagster writes under server/ stay valid across switches.

Telling whether a release folder is still in use is done in infrastructure/interface code. It reads the Dagster instance's in-progress runs (IN_PROGRESS statuses) and the folder each run recorded, for example a run tag set at run start. Domain and application stay framework-free (g6).

confirmed: horizon 17 is the release-folder switch only (5 phases); rerun only Changed Steps (rerun rules, prod fingerprints + stale-row pruning, saved adops.yaml/record state, adops run --changed in deploys, ADR-0014/0006 clarifications) is horizon 18

confirmed: server-release refuses with a message pointing at promotion.md when the new commit's top-level docker-compose.yml or server/*.yaml differ from the live copies; updating them is a manual step
confirmed: the validated checkout is mounted read-only at /checkout for server-release
confirmed: the release copy skips .git, .env and .adops; cleanup deletes nothing if any in-progress run has no release tag; only ADOPS_PROJECT points at /project/current, workspace.yaml is unchanged

Every run (scheduled, deploy, hand, Branch) is tagged adops/release with its resolved project folder; cleanup protects only tagged folders under releases/, ignores tags outside it (Branch checkouts), and deletes nothing while an untagged in-progress run exists (healed at the gate)
risks: Dagster's run worker and code server load `adops.interface.server:defs` from workspace.yaml's working_directory. If that path is /project/current, the daemon or a run worker may resolve it lazily, or again on a retry (RetryRequested re-runs run(name)). The run would then read new files partway through. The resolved path must be fixed once at run start and carried through retries (a run tag or an explicit realpath), and this is not yet verified against Dagster 1.13.

Deploy runs execute in-process and show up as Dagster runs. A scheduled run can also be waiting 3x300 s for a retry while its status stays STARTED. Both must count as 'in use' when choosing which release folders to delete, or cleanup will delete a folder a run still needs.

Atomically switching a symlink (rename over 'current') through a Docker bind mount may behave differently on OrbStack or Docker Desktop on macOS than on Linux. A Postgres-Warehouse Server may run on macOS (h16 decision), so the Mac guide must be re-checked.

Stale fingerprint rows (upserted with max+1 order and never deleted) make the first index differ after a Step is removed or renamed. Without pruning or a by-name comparison, every later deploy reruns the whole Pipeline, and Branch deferral against stage is affected too.

Running only Changed Steps means unchanged Sync Steps no longer refresh on each merge. A scheduled Pipeline's data stays as fresh as its Schedule. This changes behaviour users saw before and must be documented. Incremental cursors stay correct.

Moving prod to fingerprint-based reruns means the first prod deploy after upgrade runs everything. A wrong fingerprint saved in prod (for example under a mixed version) would silently skip a needed rerun. The per-run folder lock exists to prevent that.

Many unit tests in tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py fix the old deploy step order, the exact git fetch/checkout lines and `adops run --all --env <env>` as the second-to-last step. They must be rewritten in the same change (g7), and the real-git script test must be replaced with one for the switch script.

The h8 decision 'update the Server Project folder by local git fetch, reload, then run --all' and the h7 decision 'Server built from a bind-mounted Project' stand. The new layout must keep the bind-mounted Project (the Server folder) and only change what sits inside it, or a decision is broken without the user's say.
The h8 decision 'adops run --all takes the Warehouse lock once per Pipeline' stands. The changed-only run must keep per-Pipeline locking, not hold one lock for the whole deploy.

The new e2e case (a held scheduled run plus a deploy) must reuse the session-scoped server_image fixture and fit the 20-minute e2e job (g4). Building a second image or a real git remote could push it over.

Old-layout detection must be exact: an old-layout folder, a half-migrated folder and a fresh Server all need a defined outcome. Otherwise a deploy may change live files or refuse a correctly migrated Server.
Disk use: three releases plus checkouts on a small Server or Mac host. The user was burned by a full disk before, so the playbook should note the size.
outOfScope: Rerunning only Changed Steps on deploy (prod fingerprints, stale fingerprint pruning, adops.yaml/record state, adops run --changed, ADR-0014/0006 clarifications): held for horizon 18 to keep this horizon within 7 phases; deploys keep running every Pipeline until then.
Waiting for the Server to be idle or pausing Schedules/the QueuedRunCoordinator during a deploy: the user chose the folder switch, and deploys never wait.
Restarting or recreating Server containers on deploy: ADR-0014 and the existing unit test forbid it, and the switch happens inside the stable mount.
Automatic migration of existing Servers to the releases/current layout: the user chose one-time manual steps in promotion.md plus a clear stop message.
A rollback command, or keeping more than 3 releases for manual rollback: deleting all but the newest 3 is cleanup only, and a guided rollback is separate work.
A Step dependency graph (rerunning only a Changed Step's real dependents and skipping later independent Steps): Changed Steps keep the existing 'first changed Step onward' meaning.
Treating .env or Secret changes as a reason to rerun: .env is not in Git and is shared across releases, so a deploy cannot see a change to it.
Changing how Branch runs pick Changed Steps or which Environment they defer to: Branch runs keep comparing against stage only.
Changes to the CLI's `adops run --all` for hand use: it keeps running every Pipeline. Only deploys switch to the changed-only option.
Running Changed Steps on a Schedule tick: scheduled runs still run the whole Pipeline, and only deploys become incremental.
A prod Server e2e test or a real-runner trial of the new deploy: CI e2e covers stage only (h16 decision protects the 20-minute job). A real-runner retrial can be a later manual trial.
Freshness alerts for Pipelines that are no longer refreshed on merge: these are MAP #19, the next candidate.
Fixing the first PR's red Branch run ('stage has no Step Fingerprints') message, and the adops-stage run that starts on push before the runner exists: separate open discoveries, not this task.
Several Environments or Servers per machine: h16 decision of one Server per machine stands.
analysis.domainShapeReason: Every phase of this horizon is file-system, container and workflow mechanics for deploys (release folders, an atomic link switch, run pinning); the Promotion business rules for which Steps a deploy reruns are held for horizon 18, which is business-shaped.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: GitOps deploy of a merged or released commit to the stage or prod Server through the generated adops-stage/adops-prod workflows on that Server's self-hosted runner.

The long-lived Dagster daemon+webserver for exactly one Environment (stage or prod). It runs Schedules from the bind-mounted Server folder, which now holds releases/<commit> folders and a 'current' link.
releases/<commit>: one checked-out version of the Project inside the Server folder, sharing .env and .adops/. A run uses one release folder for its whole life.

sha256 of a Step's canonical JSON (plus the dbt tree for a Transform), saved per Pipeline and Step in the Environment's Warehouse adops schema after the Step's Checks pass. It is now saved in prod as well as stage.
A named target (dev, stage, prod, or a Branch Environment) with its own Warehouse and settings. A deploy compares fingerprints only within its own Environment.
A YAML-defined, ordered list of Sync/Transform/Reverse Sync Steps, which may have a Schedule. A Pipeline with no Schedule always runs in full on deploy.

discoveryFindings.area: server runtime: containers and mount
discoveryFindings.finding: Both dagster_daemon and dagster_webserver (YAML anchor *server, profile server) bind-mount `./:/project` from the compose project directory, with DAGSTER_HOME=/project/server and ADOPS_PROJECT=/project. The deploy's validate, `adops run --all` and chown steps are also `docker compose --project-directory "$ADOPS_SERVER_DIR" run dagster_daemon` containers using that same mount.
discoveryFindings.implication: ADOPS_SERVER_DIR is both the compose project directory and the bind-mount source. The plain template (src/adops/templates/plain/docker-compose.yml) is identical here, so both must change together.

discoveryFindings.area: server runtime: run launcher and code loading
discoveryFindings.finding: server/dagster.yaml sets QueuedRunCoordinator with max_concurrent_runs: 1 and no run_launcher, so the DefaultRunLauncher is used. workspace.yaml loads python_module adops.interface.server:defs with working_directory /project, so each run worker imports defs from disk when it starts (load_definitions runs validate_project and reads adops.yaml and every pipelines/*.yaml).
discoveryFindings.implication: A run that starts after a checkout fully uses the new version. Only reads made while a run is in progress can mix versions, and the plan must target those.

discoveryFindings.area: server runtime: when files are read during a run
discoveryFindings.finding: The op calls run_in_environment (interface/run_command.py:407). That reads adops.yaml, pipelines/<name>.yaml and .env first (line 419), then waits up to 30 min for the Warehouse lock (line 441). Inside the lock it reads pipelines/accepted/ (load_project_records, line 438), and for stage it reads the dbt tree to compute fingerprints when the plan is built (_saving_fingerprints, run_pipeline.py:645). dbtRunner then reads /project/<step.project> only when the Transform Step runs (dbt_transform.py:136).
discoveryFindings.implication: A checkout during a run can give one run old Pipeline YAML with new records or dbt, and save a stage fingerprint of tree A while dbt ran tree B. Saved Step Fingerprints become wrong, which breaks both Branch deferral and any 'rerun only Changed Steps' design.

discoveryFindings.area: server runtime: retries re-read files
discoveryFindings.finding: On a retryable failure the op raises RetryRequested (3 retries, 300 s apart) and re-runs run(name), which re-reads every Project file.
discoveryFindings.implication: One Dagster run can last 15+ minutes across retries and see different versions. Any idle wait must count a run waiting for a retry as busy (its status stays STARTED).

discoveryFindings.area: conflict: symlink or new-folder switch needs a container restart
discoveryFindings.finding: The bind-mount source `./` is resolved when the container is created, so repointing ADOPS_SERVER_DIR or a symlink to it does not change what running daemon/webserver containers see. ADR-0014 (clarification 2026-11-21) and promotion.md reject restarting the Server because it kills runs in progress, and the unit test test_deploys_reload_the_server_without_restarting_its_containers forbids compose up/down/restart/stop/start.
discoveryFindings.implication: A 'new folder and switch' design must switch inside the stable mount, for example /project/current -> releases/<sha> with a relative symlink and workspace.yaml working_directory pointing there. Otherwise it must restart only when idle, which needs an ADR-0014 amendment and a changed unit test.

discoveryFindings.area: conflict: the compose project name comes from the folder name
discoveryFindings.finding: Neither compose template sets a top-level `name:`, so the compose project name (and with it the named volumes dagster_meta_data, warehouse_data and shop_data, and the container names) comes from the basename of ADOPS_SERVER_DIR.
discoveryFindings.implication: Running compose from a new per-version folder would create a new compose project with empty Dagster run history and empty demo databases. The plan must keep a stable compose project directory, or pin `name:` or `-p`.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: persisted state location shared across versions
discoveryFindings.finding: present. Git-ignored state sits in the Project folder: .env; .adops/dlt/<env> (dlt state and Incremental cursors, dlt_sync.py:78); DuckDB Warehouse files and their .lock files (.adops/warehouse_*.duckdb, warehouse_lock.py:56); Run Logs at .adops/logs/<env> (run_log_store.py:9); Dagster compute logs at .adops/dagster/compute_logs. Dagster run, schedule and event storage is Postgres in the dagster_meta volume, and the trial notes in promotion.md mention root-owned files Dagster writes into server/logs.
discoveryFindings.implication: Every version folder must share .env and .adops/, by symlink or by mounting the shared .adops over it. server/ is tracked in Git (workspace.yaml, dagster.yaml) but gets runtime files written into it, so where DAGSTER_HOME points needs a decision.

discoveryFindings.area: precedent: running from a separate checkout that shares .adops
discoveryFindings.finding: The validate step and the pull-request workflow already run adops from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, mounted at /project, with `-v "$ADOPS_SERVER_DIR/.adops:/project/.adops"`, and the Branch run (`adops run --all --branch`) executes from that fresh checkout.
discoveryFindings.implication: The deploy's own stage/prod run could run from the validated checkout with the shared .adops and .env, without touching the live folder. Only the Server's scheduled runs then need the switch.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: a way to query in-progress runs
discoveryFindings.finding: present. dagster_server.py defines IN_PROGRESS (QUEUED, NOT_STARTED, STARTING, STARTED) and STALE; the schedule's evaluate calls instance.get_runs(RunsFilter(...)), and clear_stale_runs and recover_command.py open DagsterInstance.get() from the daemon container. The only GraphQL use is the reloadRepositoryLocation curl in the workflows.
discoveryFindings.implication: An `adops server-idle`/wait command can follow the server-recover pattern: an interface command that calls an infrastructure function. It must stay out of domain/application (guard g6) and be fully covered by unit tests (guard g2).

discoveryFindings.area: deploy runs show up as Dagster runs
discoveryFindings.finding: The deploy's `adops run` uses DagsterOrchestrator.execute_in_process against DagsterInstance.get(). In demo that instance is the root dagster.yaml (via _dagster_environ); in plain it is DAGSTER_HOME=/project/server. Both point at the same Postgres, with job name = Pipeline name, and the run bypasses the QueuedRunCoordinator.
discoveryFindings.implication: An idle check by status would also see the deploy's own in-process runs, and those runs do not take the single run slot. Only the per-Pipeline Warehouse lock keeps them apart from scheduled runs.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: stopping scheduled launches during the switch without killing runs
discoveryFindings.finding: unknown. No code pauses Schedules or the QueuedRunCoordinator. Schedules are default_status RUNNING, and clear_stale_runs' docstring says runs execute only inside the daemon container (the DefaultRunLauncher's run workers are subprocesses there), so stopping the daemon container kills runs in progress.
discoveryFindings.implication: Without a pause, 'wait for idle' has a race: a Schedule tick or a queued run can launch between the idle check and the checkout. The plan must close it by switching atomically (a symlink rename), by pausing Schedules over GraphQL or the instance (not yet verified against Dagster 1.13), or by reading files only inside the lock.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: Warehouse lock usable as an idle barrier
discoveryFindings.finding: present, but not enough on its own. warehouse_lock is a Postgres session advisory lock (fixed key) or flock on <duckdb>.lock, waiting up to 30 min. It is taken per Pipeline run in _holding_lock after adops.yaml, the Pipeline YAML and .env are read and before records, the plan and fingerprints. `run --all` takes it once per Pipeline, and Branch runs and drop-branch share stage's lock.
discoveryFindings.implication: A deploy holding the lock during checkout still leaves a waiting run with old Pipeline text and new dbt/records. To reuse the lock, move all Project file reads (including run-worker defs) inside it. Even then, a run that is between two of its Steps does not hold a lock the deploy can see.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: Step Fingerprints saved in stage
discoveryFindings.finding: present. saves_stage_fingerprint(env) is true only for "stage". FingerprintSavingStep saves each Step's fingerprint to <stage warehouse>.adops._adops_step_fingerprints right after that Step (Checks included) passes. A fingerprint is sha256 of the canonical Step JSON, plus the dbt project tree for a Transform (minus target/logs/dbt_packages/.adops/*.pyc).
discoveryFindings.implication: 'Stage reruns only Changed Steps' can compare current_fingerprints(new version) with WarehouseFingerprintStore.load(pipeline) from stage, and reuse first_changed_step. Stage must still save fingerprints for the Steps it reruns.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: Step Fingerprints in prod
discoveryFindings.finding: missing. Prod never saves fingerprints (saves_stage_fingerprint is stage only), and the store is only ever built for STAGE or the deploy Environment, with no prod comparison path.
discoveryFindings.implication: For prod to rerun only Changed Steps, prod must start saving its own fingerprints in prod's Warehouse adops schema. The first prod deploy, with no rows, must run everything; Branch runs keep reading stage only.

discoveryFindings.area: Changed Steps semantics: first changed Step onward
discoveryFindings.finding: first_changed_step returns the index of the first Step whose (name, fingerprint) pair differs in Step order. A Branch run reruns every Step from that index on (steps[first:]) and defers the earlier ones (StepStatus.DEFERRED); there is no dependency graph. plan_branch_run raises StageNotRunError when stage has no rows.
discoveryFindings.implication: Stage can reuse run_pipeline's existing `first` slicing, but with stage's default schemas instead of a Branch's; read_layout is Branch-only. It needs an output wording other than 'deferred to stage' and a choice for an unchanged Pipeline (skip it, or record a 'nothing changed' Run Log).

discoveryFindings.area: conflict: stale fingerprint rows and ordering
discoveryFindings.finding: _save upserts by (pipeline, step) with saved_order = max+1 and never deletes rows. A removed or renamed Step keeps its old low saved_order, so load() returns it first and every later comparison differs at index 0.
discoveryFindings.implication: Once a Step is removed, a 'stage reruns only Changed Steps' deploy would rerun the whole Pipeline on every deploy. The plan should prune rows for Steps no longer in the Pipeline after a passing run, or compare by name.

discoveryFindings.area: conflict: Changes that never change a fingerprint
discoveryFindings.finding: Fingerprints cover only Step JSON and the dbt tree. adops.yaml (Sources, Warehouse, Targets), .env and accepted-change records (decisions.md 2026-11-22: records 'never change Step Fingerprints') are not covered, and records are applied only when a Sync Step runs.
discoveryFindings.implication: A deploy that only adds an accepted-change record or edits adops.yaml would rerun nothing, and the record would wait for the next Schedule. The plan must decide whether a new record for a Pipeline or a settings change counts as a change.

discoveryFindings.area: conflict: Pipelines with no Schedule and Incremental Syncs
discoveryFindings.finding: ADR-0014 says 'a Pipeline with no Schedule runs only then' (on deploy), and its 2026-11-21 clarification says deploy runs every Pipeline. A skipped Sync Step keeps its dlt Incremental cursor in .adops/dlt/<env>, so its data only goes stale until the next run, with nothing corrupted.
discoveryFindings.implication: Running only Changed Steps means an unscheduled Pipeline no longer refreshes on every merge. The plan must accept and document that or keep a full run for unscheduled Pipelines, and amend the ADR-0014 clarification.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: a CLI option to run only Changed Steps
discoveryFindings.finding: missing. `adops run` (interface/run_command.py:219) has only PIPELINE, --all, --env, --branch and --project, and there is no --changed or similar anywhere in src/adops. --branch cannot be combined with --env (BRANCH_WITH_ENV).
discoveryFindings.implication: Add a new option (for example `--changed`, valid only with --env stage|prod) and route it through run_pipeline's existing `first` parameter, with 100% branch coverage (guard g2).

discoveryFindings.area: needs: the daemon picks up a code reload
discoveryFindings.finding: present (recorded in docs, not in code). promotion.md says the daemon refreshes its copy every 60 seconds, and the 2026-11-27 trial saw a new Schedule picked up without a restart. Because python_module code is loaded from disk, the daemon's code server and the run workers read the files in the bind mount directly.
discoveryFindings.implication: A switch inside the mount (symlink) is picked up by new runs without a restart. The reload step must keep pointing at location name `adops.interface.server:defs`, which the unit test derives from workspace.yaml.

discoveryFindings.area: tests: unit tests that parse the workflows
discoveryFindings.finding: tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py (DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS, lines 37-40, 858-1080) parses the generated stage/prod YAML. It asserts step order validate < folder update < reload < `adops run --all --env <env>` == second-to-last step, the exact git fetch/checkout lines (and runs that script against real git repos), the reload GraphQL text, and that no compose up/down/restart is used.
discoveryFindings.implication: These tests must be rewritten in the same change (guard g7). test_folder_update_moves_the_server_to_the_new_version_and_keeps_its_local_files should become a test that the new switch script keeps .env and .adops.

discoveryFindings.area: tests: e2e coverage of Server and deploy
discoveryFindings.finding: tests/e2e/test_server.py covers a scheduled stage run and crash recovery (server-recover), and test_demo_sync.py covers Branch deferral and two stage runs not overlapping on the Warehouse. No e2e test runs the deploy workflow steps (reload, checkout, run --all) or a deploy during a run in progress, and promotion.md's trials list that case as untried.
discoveryFindings.implication: Add an e2e test that holds a scheduled run (for example with the existing held_postgres_lock/held_duckdb_lock fixtures), runs the deploy steps and asserts the run's files did not change. It must fit the 20-minute e2e job (guard g4).

discoveryFindings.area: docs to update
discoveryFindings.finding: Docs that describe the deploy: promotion.md ('What the workflows do' table, 'After a deploy', the Warehouse lock section, Recorded trials); ADR-0016 (the deploy flow and 'one Warehouse lock'); ADR-0014's 2026-11-21 clarification ('runs every Pipeline') and its 'Pipeline with no Schedule' consequence; ADR-0006's Changed Step definition (stage only); decisions.md; docs/playbooks/run-stage-and-prod-on-a-mac.md; the comment headers of the workflows.
discoveryFindings.implication: The plan needs a docs phase: amend ADR-0014/0016 with a dated clarification, extend the Changed Step wording in ADR-0006 to stage/prod deploys, and update both playbooks. MAP.md row 18 is the source of the task.

discoveryFindings.area: guard g7: generated workflows verified by parsing YAML
discoveryFindings.finding: Applies: the task changes src/adops/templates/github/workflows/adops-stage.yml and adops-prod.yml.
discoveryFindings.implication: Every new or changed workflow step (idle wait, folder switch, changed-only run) must be asserted by parsing the generated YAML in tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py.

discoveryFindings.area: guard g2 and g5: 100% coverage, no pragma
discoveryFindings.finding: Applies to any new src/adops code: the idle-check command, the changed-only option, fingerprint saving in prod and pruning of stale rows.
discoveryFindings.implication: Each new branch needs unit tests (fake DagsterInstance, fake fingerprint store). `pragma: no cover` is not allowed except for TYPE_CHECKING.

discoveryFindings.area: guard g6: no framework in domain or application
discoveryFindings.finding: Applies: the changed-step planning belongs in application/run_pipeline.py or domain/branch_environment.py, while the Dagster run query and any lock use must stay in infrastructure/interface.
discoveryFindings.implication: Put the 'is the Server idle' logic behind a port, or keep it in infrastructure/dagster_server.py plus an interface command; never import dagster, dlt or typer into domain/application.

discoveryFindings.area: guard g3 and g4: templates in the wheel, e2e in 20 min
discoveryFindings.finding: Applies if new template files are added (for example a deploy helper script or a changed workspace.yaml/compose), and to any new e2e Server test.
discoveryFindings.implication: New template files must be included in the wheel and written by init_command (SERVER_CONFIG_FILES / _write_workflow_files). New e2e cases must reuse the session-scoped server_image fixture to stay inside the 20-minute job.

repoGuards.enforces: unit tests pass with 100% line+branch coverage of the adops package
project templates ship in the built wheel
demo Project end to end in Docker passes within the 20-minute e2e job
no pragma: no cover except TYPE_CHECKING
domain and application layers import no framework (dlt, dagster, typer, os.environ); engines sit behind ports
generated workflows are verified by parsing the generated YAML in unit tests

phases.name: Pin each Server run to its release folder
phases.goal: A Server run (scheduled or retried) resolves the Project path once when its run worker starts, records that resolved release folder on the run, and reads adops.yaml, pipelines/*.yaml, pipelines/accepted/, .env and the dbt tree only from that folder for its whole life, retries included, even if the 'current' link is switched while it runs. The deploy's own in-process `adops run` carries the same tag.
phases.rationale: Later phases will switch a 'current' symlink (a file that points at another folder) to a new release folder while runs are still going. That is only safe if a run that already started keeps reading its old folder. Nobody has checked yet whether Dagster's run worker and its retries resolve the path once or again later, so this phase proves it first, against Dagster's real loader. phases.name: Test a deploy during a held scheduled run
phases.goal: One e2e case proves that a scheduled stage run held on the Warehouse lock finishes on the old release's files and saves the old Step Fingerprint, while the next run uses the new release, and that the held run's folder is not deleted.
phases.rationale: Unit tests prove the parts; only a real Server container shows the whole deploy is safe while a run is in progress, which promotion.md lists as untried. It reuses the existing lock-holding fixtures and the session-scoped Server image so it fits the 20-minute e2e job.
changes: Build the Server folder in the new layout with commit A as 'current' and at least 3 newer dummy release folders, so commit A's folder can survive cleanup only because the held run uses it; prepare commit B changing one Pipeline.
Hold the stage Warehouse lock with held_postgres_lock/held_duckdb_lock, let a scheduled run start and wait, then run the deploy steps (server-release for commit B and the code reload).
Release the lock and assert the held run's Run Log and saved stage Step Fingerprint match commit A, releases/<A> still exists, and the next run uses commit B.
Reuse the session-scoped server_image fixture; build no second image and use no remote Git.
inputs: Phase deploy-workflows-use-release-folders: new layout fixture and workflow steps
Phase pin-run-to-release-folder: run tag and pinning
DISCOVERY: held_postgres_lock/held_duckdb_lock fixtures and server_image exist in tests/e2e
phases.expectedResult: A passing e2e test in tests/e2e/test_server.py showing a held scheduled run finishes on the old release folder while the next run uses the new one.
guardNotes: g4: reuses session-scoped server_image and existing lock fixtures; one added case measured to keep the e2e job under 20 minutes

rubric.label: Held run completes on commit A's files and fingerprint
rubric.ruleStatement: A scheduled stage run that started and is waiting on the held Warehouse lock, when released after commit B is deployed, finishes using commit A's Pipeline definition and saves commit A's Step Fingerprint.
passCriteria: `uv run pytest tests/e2e/test_server.py -m e2e -k held -v` passes
The test asserts the held run's Run Log contains a marker unique to commit A's changed Pipeline and the saved stage Step Fingerprint equals the fingerprint computed from commit A's Step, not B's
The test asserts the held run's adops/release tag names releases/<A>
The test confirms the run had actually STARTED (resolved its folder) before the deploy, e.g. by polling run status before calling server-release
failureExamples: The run is still QUEUED when the deploy happens, so it legitimately starts on B and the test asserts nothing about pinning
Commit A and B differ only in a comment, so fingerprints are equal and the assertion is vacuous
The lock is released before server-release finishes, so the run completes before the switch

rubric.label: Cleanup really had to spare the held folder
rubric.ruleStatement: At deploy time at least 3 release folders newer than A exist, so releases/<A> survives only because the held run uses it, and it still exists after the deploy.
passCriteria: The test creates ≥3 dummy release folders with creation/mtime later than A (set explicitly with os.utime or ordered creation) before deploy
After server-release, the test asserts releases/<A> exists and at least one other old dummy folder was deleted (proving cleanup ran)
`grep -n 'utime\|releases' tests/e2e/test_server.py tests/e2e/conftest.py` shows the folder timing set up
failureExamples: Only 1 or 2 newer folders exist, so keep-newest-3 saves A and the in-use path is never exercised
Dummy folders are named so they sort after A but created before it; cleanup sorts by time and A is newest anyway
Cleanup never ran (deletes nothing) because an untagged run existed, and the test passes for the wrong reason

rubric.label: The next run uses commit B
rubric.ruleStatement: A run started after the deploy uses releases/<B>: its tag names B and its Run Log or fingerprint reflects B's change.
passCriteria: The test triggers or waits for a run after the held one and asserts its adops/release tag names releases/<B> and its Run Log shows B's marker
The test asserts /project/current inside the container reads `releases/<B>` (docker exec readlink)
failureExamples: The code location is not reloaded, so the next run still uses A's definitions and the test only checks the tag
Test reads the link from the host only, missing a container-side mismatch

rubric.label: Reuses shared fixtures and stays within the e2e job
rubric.ruleStatement: The case uses the session-scoped server_image and held_postgres_lock/held_duckdb_lock fixtures, builds no new image, uses no remote Git, and the full e2e job still finishes inside 20 minutes.
passCriteria: `grep -n 'server_image\|held_postgres_lock\|held_duckdb_lock' tests/e2e/test_server.py` shows the new test uses them; `grep -n 'docker build\|git clone\|git push' tests/e2e/test_server.py` finds nothing new
`uv run pytest tests/e2e -m e2e --durations=10` shows the new case's time and the total under 20 minutes
Waits use bounded polling with a timeout, not fixed long sleeps
failureExamples: Test waits on the real 300 s retry backoff, adding 5+ minutes
A fixed time.sleep(60) to 'let the schedule tick' instead of polling run status
The new case rebuilds the image with a different tag for commit B

phases.healerHint: Most likely the deploy happens before the scheduled run has actually started (still QUEUED), making the test vacuous or flaky; poll the Dagster run status until STARTED with the lock held before calling server-release.

successCriteria: Done when ALL hold, each proved by a unit test that parses the generated YAML (g7) or by code covered 100% line+branch with no new pragma (g2/g5), plus one e2e case inside the 20-minute job (g4): (1) adops-stage.yml and adops-prod.yml never run git fetch/checkout into the live Server folder and never compose up/down/restart/stop/start; they validate, run `adops server-release` with the validated checkout mounted read-only at /checkout, reload `adops.interface.server:defs`, then run every Pipeline from /project/current. (2) Bind mount, compose project directory and compose project name are unchanged by a switch, so Dagster run history and demo data survive. (3) A run resolves 'current' once at start and reads adops.yaml, pipelines/, pipelines/accepted/, .env and the dbt tree only from that folder for its whole life, retries included; one e2e case holds a scheduled stage run, deploys a new commit, and shows the held run finishes on the old files and fingerprint while the next run uses the new ones. (4) After a switch, every release folder except the newest 3, the current one and any folder a run in progress uses is deleted; a run in progress never loses its folder (the e2e makes ≥3 newer folders so this is really tested). (5) server-release stops before changing any file on the old or half-moved layout, and when the new commit's docker-compose.yml or server/*.yaml differ from the live top-level copies, each time naming the matching section of docs/playbooks/promotion.md, which gives the one-time manual move and the manual config-update step. (6) ADR-0016 has a dated clarification; promotion.md, run-stage-and-prod-on-a-mac.md and the workflow headers describe the new flow. (7) Plain and demo templates change together, templates ship in the wheel (g3), ruff passes (g1).

Pin each Server run to its release folder: A passing unit test that loads the Server code location through Dagster's real loader, switches 'current' mid-run, and shows the run and its retry read only the release folder resolved at run start and tag the run with it.

Add release folder layout check, switch and cleanup: src/adops/infrastructure/release_folders.py with unit tests covering layout detection, release preparation, atomic 'current' switch and cleanup selection at 100% line+branch.

Add a Server release command: A working `adops server-release` command with unit tests proving it refuses the old layout without changing files, switches 'current', and never deletes a folder a run in progress uses.

Change deploys to switch release folders: Generated stage and prod deploy workflows that switch release folders, verified by rewritten YAML-parsing unit tests in tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py.
Test a deploy during a held scheduled run: A passing e2e test in tests/e2e/test_server.py showing a held scheduled run finishes on the old release folder while the next run uses the new one.
deferred: Rerunning only Changed Steps on deploy (prod fingerprints, stale fingerprint pruning, adops.yaml/record state, adops run --changed, ADR-0014/0006 clarifications): held for horizon 18 to keep this horizon within 7 phases; deploys keep running every Pipeline until then.
Waiting for the Server to be idle or pausing Schedules/the QueuedRunCoordinator during a deploy: the user chose the folder switch, and deploys never wait.
Restarting or recreating Server containers on deploy: ADR-0014 and the existing unit test forbid it, and the switch happens inside the stable mount.
Automatic migration of existing Servers to the releases/current layout: the user chose one-time manual steps in promotion.md plus a clear stop message.
A rollback command, or keeping more than 3 releases for manual rollback: deleting all but the newest 3 is cleanup only, and a guided rollback is separate work.
A Step dependency graph (rerunning only a Changed Step's real dependents and skipping later independent Steps): Changed Steps keep the existing 'first changed Step onward' meaning.
Treating .env or Secret changes as a reason to rerun: .env is not in Git and is shared across releases, so a deploy cannot see a change to it.
Changing how Branch runs pick Changed Steps or which Environment they defer to: Branch runs keep comparing against stage only.
Changes to the CLI's `adops run --all` for hand use: it keeps running every Pipeline. Only deploys switch to the changed-only option.
Running Changed Steps on a Schedule tick: scheduled runs still run the whole Pipeline, and only deploys become incremental.
A prod Server e2e test or a real-runner trial of the new deploy: CI e2e covers stage only (h16 decision protects the 20-minute job). A real-runner retrial can be a later manual trial.
Freshness alerts for Pipelines that are no longer refreshed on merge: these are MAP #19, the next candidate.
Fixing the first PR's red Branch run ('stage has no Step Fingerprints') message, and the adops-stage run that starts on push before the runner exists: separate open discoveries, not this task.
Several Environments or Servers per machine: h16 decision of one Server per machine stands.
